text:
lina-support: FYI support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting 2x API p99 in eu-west since ~09:30 UTC. Customer sees spikes in inference latency ~1.2s -> 4s on some requests, affects checkout flow. They attached curl timings and trace ids. Escalating.
sara-oncall: I paged you @james-netops and @oliver-sre. Can you grab initial network traces?
james-netops: pulling egress logs for AcmeCorp tenant, route mapping for eu-west. I see a subset of requests are being egressed via us-east1 for ~8% of flows from the eu-west poP. Likely anycast/route shift.
oliver-sre: attaching quick sample from the customer's traceroute and curl -v output they pasted: 
```
$ curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
time_connect:0.180 time_appconnect:0.980 time_total:1.220
```
Note time_appconnect spikes ~0.9-1.2s on affected requests.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T09:25:40Z: edge-routing-policy v2 rolled to eu-west PoP (canary 10%).
james-netops: interesting, rollout at 09:25 matches symptom start. The canary may have mis-tagged prefixes causing BGP shift to a different egress with higher inter-region RTT.
mina-obs: logs show increased TLS handshake retries and a bump in TLS 1.3 handshake timeouts from 0.25s to ~1s on same timeframe. Session ticket acceptance rate dropped ~30%.
lina-support: Customer says it impacts their checkout latency and is "very visible" - they requested ETA on mitigation.
oliver-sre: quick checklist: 1) confirm route shift 2) confirm TLS handshake metrics per POP 3) check session ticket eviction / 0-RTT fallback behavior 4) consider immediate traffic steering.
james-netops: ran `bgp-view --prefix 203.0.113.0/24 --since 09:00` — we see AS path change: previously via AS65010 (eu provider) now through AS65199 -> us-east provider for ~8% of flows.
sara-oncall: can we repro locally? Mina, any synthetic p95 anomalies?
mina-obs: synthetic runner from eu-west1 to api endpoint shows p95 increasing from 180ms -> 1.1s on 7/1000 samples. TCP handshake fine but TLS appconnect is the spike. Here's a tcpdump snippet showing repeated ClientHello with no early ticket resume: 
```
09:32:12.123456 IP client > edge: Flags [S], seq 0
09:32:12.303789 TLS ClientHello (len=512)
09:32:13.303890 TLS ClientHello (len=512)  # retransmit after 1s 
09:32:13.304120 TLS ServerHello (len=128)
```
That 1s retransmit looks like our handshake layering waiting.
james-netops: looks like cross-az routing added ~150-200ms extra RTT; combined with server-side TLS session ticket misses -> client retries and 0-RTT fallback causing extra waits. Some clients then do full handshake which costs an extra RTT.
oliver-sre: hypothesis: the new routing policy changed upstream next-hop for some prefixes; those paths have higher latency and also sometimes drop the 0-RTT session tickets (maybe due to asymmetric path causing packets dropped), forcing full handshake and retransmission.
sara-oncall: mitigation options: 1) roll back routing policy canary; 2) force traffic away from affected egress via local steering; 3) increase handshake parallelism/disable aggressive 0-RTT fallback temporarily; 4) ask customer to use short retry/backoff. Which is fastest?
james-netops: fastest is rollback of canary or adjust origin selection to prefer eu provider. Can push rollback to remove mis-tagging in 10min.
oliver-sre: while rollback is in flight, we can also hotfix edge to accept session tickets from multiple keysets and increase session ticket cache TTL to reduce misses. That requires a small config flip — I can prepare.
mina-obs: adding: traces show higher TLS alerts 'bad_record_mac' in small percentage, consistent with MTU/fragmentation on new path — may be unrelated but worth noting.
mina-obs: dashboard panels: `tls_handshake_time.p99{pop=eu-west}` shows spike 09:25 -> 09:40 correlating with canary.
sara-oncall: OK do rollback + edge config flip. James, OLiver coordinate. Lina, keep customer updated with ETA.
james-netops: rolling back edge-routing-policy v2 in canary now. Command: `edgectl policy rollback --name edge-routing-policy --to stable` — started at 09:48 UTC.
deploy-bot: Rollback invoked by james-netops at 2026-03-15T09:48:12Z.
mina-obs: telemetry: within 120s of rollback, p95 in eu-west dropped from 1.1s -> 220ms on canary traffic. Affected customer reported partial improvement.
oliver-sre: applying session ticket TTL bump: set `tls.session_ticket.ttl = 86400` and enable backing key rotation acceptance window. Pushed config to eu-west PoP as hotfix at 09:52.
mina-obs: after both mitigations, tls_appconnect p99 back to baseline ~250ms; droppped retransmit signatures eliminated. No user-facing error counts.
lina-support: told AcmeCorp the mitigation is rolled out; they confirm 80% of sessions restored to baseline, will monitor next 24h. They asked for RCA.
sara-oncall: RCA outline: 1) edge-routing-policy v2 canary mis-tagged a subset of prefixes causing upstream egress via a higher-latency provider; 2) higher RTT + occasional packet loss caused TLS session ticket misses and handshake retransmits leading to p99 latency regressions; 3) rollback + session-ticket TTL hotfix mitigated impact.
oliver-sre: follow-ups: - add canary guardrails to compare egress AS path distribution before rollout - add synthetic checks for tls_appconnect p99 as canary gating - increase observability for session ticket acceptance rates per-pop - create runbook steps for immediate traffic steering.
james-netops: will schedule a postmortem with network infra to prevent prefix mis-tagging.
sara-oncall: filing incident task: INC-2026-0457, assigned to james-netops / oliver-sre / mina-obs. Lina, please attach customer timeline and confirm their SLA credits if any.
lina-support: added timeline and raw traces to ticket, customer thanked us for fast response and asked for weekly updates. :thumbsup:
customer-ops-bot: Customer AcmeCorp status updated: "Investigating - degraded" -> "Mitigated" at 2026-03-15T10:02:30Z.
sara-oncall: closing out here, but leave monitoring on for 72h. Good ops team work.
